summary: The study investigates the use of octadecanethiol (ODT) self-assembled monolayer (SAM) as a passivation layer to enable area-selective deposition (ASD) of HfN on Cu and SiO2 substrates. The effectiveness of ODT in blocking HfN ALD on Cu is influenced by the surface pre-treatment of Cu, with oxidized Cu surfaces showing better inhibition. The results highlight the importance of surface properties in determining the success of ASD processes.
evidence: The results stress the essential contribution of interface properties in forming dense thiol-SAM on metals, which is fundamental to a successful ASD process. It is here demonstrated that ODT on clean Cu cannot block HfN ALD at 150 °C, whereas on oxidized Cu the same organic layer prevents up to 19 nm HfN film growth before the Cu passivation is affected.
